newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down acoss the board in slow trade on Friday on profit-taking by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 22,850 yuan ($2,755) per tonne, losing 50 yuan. It opened at 22,930 yuan and hit a high of 22,960 yuan.
May fell 150 to 23,050, June 120 to 22,980, July 60 to 22,870 and September 70 to 22,860 yuan.
Combined volume fell sharply to 14,330 from 31,600 tonnes.
Copper opened mixed but profit-taking pushed prices steadily down for most of the session before most contracts closing at their intraday lows.
Traders said many investors preferred to stay on the sidelines as the weekend approached, and this compounded the slow trade.
"Most investors are reluctant to hold long positions at the weekend, especially at present when market sentiment is weak," one trader said.
"The outlook is not optimistic in the short term despite the support of firm physical copper prices," he said.
Physical copper was fetching around 23,300 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Traders said many investors were disappointed with copper's recent performance on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and that Shanghai copper futures could not hold at the current highs for too long.
"If LME copper can not boost the confidence of Shanghai's long position holders, then we'll probably see the local market test 22,500 yuan in the next few days," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down across the board. May fell 80 to 15,370, June 100 to 15,500 and July 200 to 15,600 yuan.
Combined volume rose to 1,290 tonnes from 160 tonnes.
